questions.question:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

We have to always be on our (1)/guard to ensure the highest level (2)/of safety inside train operations. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the placement of the adverb "always."
 
• The correct rule states that **adverbs of frequency, such as "always,"** should be placed directly after the first auxiliary verb if there is more than one verb in the sentence.
 
• In this case, **"have" i**s the auxiliary verb that precedes the base verb** "be."**
 
• Therefore, the correct phrasing should be "We always have to be on our guard." 
 
• Thus the correct option is 1 and therefore the answer.

questions.question: If ‘T’ means ‘+’, ‘U’ means ‘÷’, ‘V’ means ‘×’ and ‘W’ means ‘–’, then which of the following equation is true?
questions.solution:
**Letter**

 
 
 
T

 
 
 
U

 
 
 
V

 
 
 
W

 
 
 

 
 
** Meaning **

 
 
 
 +

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 
 ×

 
 
 
–

 
 
 

 

Lets’ check each option,

1) 11 V 3 U 33 T 2 = 122

Equation will become 11 × 3 ÷ 33 + 2

Now, according to BODMAS rule we have:

11 × 3 ÷ 33 + 2

= 11 × 1 ÷ 11 + 2

= 1 + 2

= 3 ≠ 122

2) 6 V 9 U 18 W 2 = 0

Equation will become 6 × 9 ÷ 18 – 2

Now, according to BODMAS rule we have:

6 × 9 ÷ 18 – 2

= 6 × 0.5 – 2

= 3 – 2

= 1 ≠ 0

3) 6 V 3 U 15 T 2 = 9/2

Equation will become 6 × 3 ÷ 15 + 2

Now, according to BODMAS rule we have:

6 × 3 ÷ 15 + 2

= 6 × (1/5) + 2

= 6/5 + 2

= (6 + 10)/5

= 16/5 ≠ 9/2

4) 12 T 4 U 2 V 16 = 44

Equation will become 12 + 4 ÷ 2 × 16

Now, according to BODMAS rule we have:

12 + 4 ÷ 2 × 16

= 12 + 2 × 16

= 12 + 32

= 44

Hence, equation 4 is true

questions.question:
If 1 × 2 × 3 = 36 and 2 × 3 × 4 = 81, then

1 × 3 × 4 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

1 × 2 × 3 = 36

→ (1 + 2 + 3)² = 6² = 36

2 × 3 × 4 = 81

(2 + 3 + 4)² = 9² = 81

Similarly,

1 × 3 × 4 → (1 + 3 + 4)² = 8² = **64**

Hence, 64 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

72, 76, 74, 78, 76, 80, 78, ?
questions.solution:
There are two series in the given series i.e. first series is 72, 74, 76, 78, ……. and second series is 76, 78, 80, ….

The pattern followed in the first series is as follows:

**72** → 72 + 2 = **74** → 74 + 2 = **76** → 76 + 2 = **78**

The pattern followed in the second series is as follows:

**76** → 76 + 2 = **78** → 78 + 2 = **80** → 80 + 2 = **82**

Hence, 82 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Present age of Usha is 36 years. 10 years ago, ratio of ages of Usha and Asha was 2 : 3. What will be Asha’s age (in years) after 2 years?
questions.solution:
Let the Asha’s present age is X years.

Usha’s present age = 36

Usha’s age 10 years ago = 36 – 10 = 26

Asha’s age 10 years ago = X – 10

Given: Ratio = 2 : 3

26 / X – 10 = 2/3

78 = 2X – 20

2X = 78 + 20

2X = 98

X = 49 (Present age)

So, Asha’s age after 2 years = X + 2 = 49 + 2 = 51 years.

Hence, 51 is the correct answer.

I. Some grapes are green.

II. Some green are colour.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some grapes are colour.

II. Some grapes are not colour.

questions.question: If N = 2³ × 3², then what are the positive factors of N?
questions.solution:

12 = 2 × 2 × 3

20 = 2 × 2 × 5

Out of the above numbers, 12 is only one with factors both 2 and 3

∴ 12 in positive factor of 2³ × 3².

questions.question: What is the least common multiple of 24, 48 and 72?
questions.solution:
Listing the prime factor of each number

24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3

48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3

72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

Multiply each factor the greatest number of times it occurs in any of the numbers.

48 has 4 2s, 72 has 2 3s. This gives us 144, the smallest number that can be divided evenly by 24, 48 and 72

questions.question: X, Y, and Z together can complete a work in 20 days. Y and Z can complete the same work in 30 days. In how many days can X complete the same work alone?
questions.solution:
Work done by X, Y, and Z in one day = 1/20

Work done by Y and Z in one day = 1/30

⇒ Work done by X in one day = (1/20) – (1/30) = 1/60

∴ X can complete the work alone in 60 days.

questions.question: U, V and W together can complete a work in 10 days. If U alone can complete the work in 20 days and V alone can complete the work in 30 days, then in how many days W alone can complete the work?
questions.solution:
1 day work of U, V and W = 1/10

1 day work of U = 1/20

1 day work of V = 1/30(3)

⇒ 1 day work of W = (1/10) - (1/20) - (1/30) = 1/60

∴ W can complete the work in 60 days.

questions.question: Average weight of P and Q is 32 kg. Average weight of Q and R is 43 kg. Average weight of P and R is 51 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of P, Q and R?
questions.solution:
∵ Average weight of P and Q is 32 kg

⇒ P + Q = 64 kg (1)

Similarly,

questions.question: Raman goes office at a speed of 40 kmph and returns home at a speed of 60 kmph. What is his average speed (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
Let the distance between Raman’s office and home is x km

Speed = distance/time

Time = distance/speed

Time taken to go to office, t₁ = x/40

Time taken to return to home, t₂ = x/60

Total time taken = t₁ + t₂ = x/40 + x/60 = x/24

Total distance travelled = 2x

Average speed = total distance travelled/total time taken = (2x)/(x/24) = 48 kmph

questions.question: A certain amount is invested in a scheme of simple interest. It amounts to Rs. 3096 in 6 years and Rs. 3744 in 9 years. What is the rate of interest (in percentage)?
questions.solution:
Simple interest = S.I = (principle × rate × time)/100

Let the principle be p

Rate of interest be r

After 6 years,

Amount = p + S.I

⇒ p + (p × r × 6)/100 = 3096

⇒ 100p + 6 × r × p - 309600 = 0(1)

After 9 years,

Amount = p + S.I

⇒ p + (p × r × 9)/100 = 3744

⇒ 100p + 9 × r × p - 374400 = 0(2)

Solving equation (1) and (2)

p = 1800 and r = 12

∴ rate of interest = 12%

questions.question: During photosynthesis the oxygen in glucose comes from ______.

options.text: Both from water and carbon dioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis is the physiochemical process, in which carbohydrates (organic compounds) are formed from inorganic substrates like H₂O & CO₂ in the presence of light and pigments.
 
• O₂ is evolved as a by-product during photosynthesis.
 
• The **oxygen molecule present in glucose is derived from carbon dioxide** during **Calvin cycle of photosynthesis**.
 
• The CO₂ molecule is first added to 3-phosphoglycerate during the carboxylation reaction of Calvin cycle, and is later used to form glucose.
 
• While molecular oxygen that is liberated during photosynthesis is produced from photolysis of water during the light reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis can be simply divided into 4 major processes

 
• Absorption of light energy by **Chlorophyll pigment.**
 
• Conversion of light energy into chemical energy.
 
• **Splitting of water or Photolysis** during Non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

** H₂O → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻⁻ + [IMAGE: file:///C:/Users/utkar/AppData/Local/Temp/OICE_7537A668-6D1D-4E05-8EA6-84C3B2569657.0/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image004.png] O₂ **↑

**The oxygen that evolved during this process comes from water__**.

 
• **Reduction of CO₂ to carbohydrates (Glucose) during Dark reaction.**

**​**The CO2 undergoes reduction and its O2 is utilized in the formation of Glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

The **O₂ released during photolysis is the evolved O₂**, whereas **the O₂ released during the reduction of CO₂ is the O₂ in glucose.**
